This receptor subunit is then linked to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 2B1, suggesting a potential pathway where Novobiocin may modulate the activity of this transporter. The evidence implies a possible role for Novobiocin in influencing the transport of anionic compounds, possibly through interactions with the receptor subunit, which in turn affects the transporter's function. The integration of these relationships highlights a possible mechanism where Novobiocin could modulate the transport of organic anions via a receptor-dependent pathway, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
